### Fixes
- Notes with newline-separated preferences or facts now keep each claim in
  stored summaries without splitting wrapped lines into separate statements.
- Embedded project-scoped writes. `longmemory_ingest` with a `project_id`,
  `longmemory_remember_decision` and connector imports go through
  `applyImportPlan`, which stored every node without a semantic vector, so
  those memories never received a vector score in recall (#216).
- The HTTP server never read `LONGMEMORY_TENANT_ID`/`LONGMEMORY_USER_ID`, so
  every restart silently re-scoped the engine (and the `/mcp` endpoint) to the
  `default` tenant and user, making memories saved under a configured scope
  unreachable after a restart (#215).
- MCP tool responses (`longmemory_ingest`, `longmemory_recall`, and others)
  embedded each node's full embedding vector, repeated across every place the
  node is nested in a response, inflating responses by thousands of tokens.
  Vectors are now stripped by default (`LONGMEMORY_MCP_INCLUDE_VECTORS=true`
  or a per-call `include_vectors: true` input restores them); ingest and
  recall responses also no longer repeat a node already returned in full

## 0.3.5
**Two community fixes: precheck recognises a file however its path is spelled, and the summary stays small even when entries are long.**
### Fixed
- **`precheck_file` called a file with known failures "Safe to modify" when its path was spelled differently.** Events store project-relative paths, so `./src/auth.py`, an absolute path, a path through a symlinked folder, a backslash path or a Windows `C:\` path matched nothing. ### Fixed
- **A resent `/memory/add` no longer cuts the same messages twice** (#274).
  Messages were deduplicated only against the session buffer, so a client
  retrying after a timeout re-sent messages the first call had already cut
  into a memory cell, and they became a second memcell and episode. The
  boundary stage now drops fresh messages a memcell of the session already
  holds. Message ids no longer depend on where a message sits in its request:
  `m_<session>_<timestamp>_<digest>`, `digest` covering who said what (a
  message repeated verbatim in one request is told apart by its repeat
  count), so a resend -- whole, split or regrouped, within one millisecond
  too -- keeps its ids, and two different messages sent in separate requests
  with one timestamp are no longer merged into one. Messages sharing a
  timestamp keep arrival order in the buffer rather than sorting by id.
  The internal helper `everos.memory.extract.ingest.gen_message_id` is
  replaced by `message_ids`. Buffered messages from an earlier version keep
  their old ids; a batch sent before the upgrade and resent after it is not
  recognized as a resend.
